skills:
Actual Minimum Requirements
Education Minimum: Not stated in posting.
Required Experience: Experience in a customer service role, preferably in a call center setting.
Preferred Experience: Call center experience.
Required Skills:
Strong mental and emotional resilience with challenging customer interactions
Excellent interpersonal and communication skills, including empathy and rapport building
Ability to multitask in a fast-paced, demanding environment
Comfortable navigating multiple software programs across multiple screens
Genuine desire to help customers find solutions
4. Best Fit
 This role is ideal for:
Someone with prior customer service experience, especially call center work, who is comfortable with a steady call volume
Someone who stays calm and kind when a caller is stressed or upset
Someone who likes explaining things clearly, like insurance coverage, in everyday language
Someone who wants a solid hourly rate with overtime eligibility and good benefits
Not a Good Fit for:
Anyone who gets worn down by emotionally heavy calls or a high daily call count
Anyone who can't work the later weekday hours or Saturday mornings
Anyone who can't commit to the full 6 week training
Top 10 Resume Keywords:
High volume inbound call handling
Insurance policy and coverage explanation
Claims inquiry support
Emotional resilience under pressure
Multitasking across multiple systems
Email and phone customer support
Cross-department collaboration
Empathy and rapport building
Policy changes and adjustments
Contact center experience
notes:
Expected Application & Interviewing Process: 1. Application 2. Expect an assessment at the end of the application or directly emailed to you. 3. If assessment is passing, expect a recruiter to reach out via email or text for a phone screen. 4. If phone screen passes you can expect the final interview. Total time to hire from date of application can be anywhere from 3-15 days on average.
4-5 interview questions for this role:
Tell us about your customer service experience, especially in a call center.
How do you stay calm and supportive when a caller is upset or going through something stressful?
How do you manage handling a high number of calls in a day while keeping each one quality?
Walk us through how you would explain a coverage question to someone who is confused about their options.
How do you feel about working a schedule that includes a Saturday morning?
other:
Pay, Shift, Benefits, Background, Drug Test Information, and Career Pathway:
Pay: $20.19/hr, confirmed in posting. Non-exempt and eligible for overtime. Not eligible for additional incentive pay.
Shift: Full-time. Monday through Friday, 10:30am to 7:00pm CST, plus Saturday 9:00am to 1:00pm CST (posted as 11:30am to 8:00pm and 10:00am to 2:00pm EST). Training lasts 6 weeks, with training hours confirmed before the class starts.
Benefits: Medical, dental, and vision insurance, company paid basic life insurance, company paid short and long term disability, 12 weeks of 100% paid parental leave, HSA and FSA, retirement savings plan, personal paid time off, paid holidays and a company wide Wellness Day off, paid time off to volunteer, group pet insurance, on the job training and skills development, and an Employee Assistance Program. Some offerings depend on work location.
Equipment Provided: Not stated in posting.
Felony Friendly?: Not stated.
Drug Test: Not stated.
Notes: The application closes October 7, 2026, so this one is time sensitive. The call volume is real and stated outright (70 to 90 calls a day), so it fits someone who already handles phones comfortably. The posting title says Customer Service Representative while the body says Customer Care Representative, so both names may show up in the application portal. Phone and video interviews may be recorded and transcribed, and applicants who give a mobile number may get text messages about the job.
Career Pathway: Not stated directly in posting, though the benefits mention opportunities for career advancement. Reasonable inferred path: Customer Care Representative → Senior Customer Care Representative → Team Lead → Contact Center Supervisor, though this is an estimate, not confirmed by Embrace directly.
training: discussed in interview/ofer stage. must be available for any shift
